title: Bangladesh seeks World Bank aid for trade reforms ahead of LDC exit
content:
Bangladesh has sought World Bank policy and technical support to streamline business procedures, digitise government services and diversify exports ahead of LDC graduation. 
The government plans a three-year reform programme, including completing business approval processes within 14 days, strengthening trade facilitation, improving customs procedures and expanding export opportunities.

title: US takes 29% of India's textile exports: Can new capacity pay off?
content:
India’s Gujarat textile policy has seen a Surat district committee approve 627 applications worth ₹1,521 crore (~$162 million) across weaving, technical textiles and embroidery.
The proposals could attract ₹300 crore in assistance over five years and more than 3,500 jobs, though figures remain estimates.
The US is India’s largest textile and apparel export market, with a 29 per cent share in FY2024–25.

title: South Indian cotton yarn remains stable, signs of better demand
content:
India’s cotton yarn prices stayed stable in Mumbai and Tiruppur after Diwali, with buying improving in Mumbai but demand still slow in Tiruppur amid payment constraints.
Traders expect summer garment manufacturing and fabric output to lift yarn consumption in coming weeks.
Gujarat cotton rose ₹500 (~$5.32) per candy as mill demand, global cues and market reopenings supported trade.

title: India-Thailand trade rises 12.6% to $21.49 bn in FY 2025-26
content:
India-Thailand trade rose 12.6 per cent year on year to $21.49 billion in FY 2025-26, with Thailand accounting for 16.7 per cent of India’s trade with ASEAN. 
At their 14th Joint Trade Committee meeting, the two countries explored textile cooperation, discussed linking UPI with PromptPay and considered ways to help traders use existing tariff preferences and overcome non-tariff barriers in both markets.

title: ICE cotton futures slump on weak demand, stronger US dollar
content:
ICE cotton futures fell sharply as weak export demand, a stronger US dollar and December liquidation weighed ahead of the November 23 first notice day.
December 2026 settled 178 points lower at 77.00 cents per pound, and total open interest fell to 349,653 contracts.
USDA said upland export sales dropped 43 per cent from the previous week; China bought just 1,994 bales.

title: 17 trade deals, $12.9 bn in fabric imports. What is Vietnam missing?
content:
Vietnam’s garment exports rose 3.9 per cent to $39.84 billion in January-October 2026, but fabric import dependence is constraining preferential tariff access.
TexPro says China, Taiwan and South Korea supplied 87.5 per cent of an $11.07-billion fabric basket in January-August; CPTPP partners supplied just 5.0 per cent.
New local output must meet buyer specifications and origin rules.

title: US' Nike to launch Tuned Air running footwear in late 2027
content:
Nike has unveiled Tuned Air, a proprietary digital-print and selective-lamination platform designed to give athletes tailored cushioning, comfort, durability and responsiveness across sports.
The technology has cut average new Air-unit development time by 70 per cent at Nike’s Advanced Product Creation Center, with runner availability planned for late 2027 before a broader rollout.

title: What drove Israel’s Delta Galil to record Q3 sales of $599.6 mn?
content:
Delta Galil Industries posted record third-quarter 2026 sales of $599.6 million, up 11 per cent YoY, as DTC revenue grew 16 per cent. 
Net income increased 17 per cent to $36.6 million and adjusted EBIT rose 23 per cent to $63.1 million. 
The Israeli apparel group expects FY26 results to reach the middle to high end of its guidance range.

title: 65 Bangladesh RMG factories shut: Can 2027 orders stay on track?
content:
Bangladesh's RMG minimum stays at Tk12,500 (~$100) until a new rate is notified, as the Minimum Wage Board considers a worker-side Tk32,000 proposal for the lowest regular grade.
The employers' proposal meeting was postponed to November 23; BGMEA reported 65 factories indefinitely closed by November 15.
RMG exports reached $38.70 billion in fiscal 2025–26, equal to 80.6 per cent of merchandise exports.

title: Bangladesh's RMG wage board to discuss wage proposal on November 23
content:
Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board will hold its third garment-sector wage meeting on November 23, after the November 16 session was postponed.
Owners' representatives had been due to submit a written minimum-wage proposal; workers' representatives earlier sought Tk32,000 (~$257) a month.
Unrest has continued in Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur over a Tk30,000 (~$241) demand.

title: Who is winning Spain’s $16 bn apparel import race?
content:
Spain’s garment imports rose 10.44 per cent to $16.08 billion in January-August 2026, even as wider EU apparel imports fell.
Bangladesh stayed Spain’s top supplier at $3.05 billion, but its share slipped to 18.99 per cent, while China, Cambodia and Turkiye gained.
Egypt’s growth was driven by men’s and women’s cotton woven bottoms, highlighting product-level shifts in Spanish sourcing.
